what_this_is: Replay sources for the claim-integrity check, one entry per must_catch finding in claim_corpus.json. All four must_catch findings are now fixed: three before this sprint opened, and I4 by sprint decision #16-C. None of them can be scored against the tree as it stands, so each pins the historical file content by git BLOB SHA, which is a content hash, so a pinned source can never drift. Kind 'worktree' stays a first-class kind for a finding that is still on disk. No entry needs it today, so the validator's worktree rules are held up by the suite's own synthetic fixtures instead.
why_blob_shas: A blob SHA is derived from the bytes themselves, so 'this content was live at that commit' is verifiable rather than asserted. Copying a snapshot into the repo would have made the fixture an unverifiable claim about history, which is the defect class this sprint exists to catch. Commits are recorded as full 40-char SHAs for the same reason: an abbreviated or relative commit-ish (ab5cb74~1) is an expression, not a pin.
worktree_means_the_worktree: kind 'worktree' means the files on disk right now, NOT the corpus term 'live_at_head' and NOT the corpus derived_at commit 2ccb728. Those are different things and conflating them is easy, so it is said here once: a worktree fixture scores what a check would see if it ran today.

field_guide.id: The finding id in claim_corpus.json. Read-only there, never written by anything here.
field_guide.kind: blobs when the defect was fixed and the content has to come from history. worktree when the defect is still on disk.
field_guide.scored_as: Which site this entry scores. Required, because corpus note n5 says whoever scores a finding must state which site they are counting.
field_guide.files: For kind blobs only. Every file the replay materialises, each pinned by blob SHA plus its byte size, both asserted after materialisation.
field_guide.path: Where the file is written inside the replay scope, and the path a witness names.
field_guide.blob: 40-char lowercase hex git blob SHA. Validated for shape, then confirmed to be a blob object, then confirmed to hash back to this value after it is read.
field_guide.size: Byte length of the blob. Asserted alongside the hash, because the failure this guards is a silently EMPTY file, which an absent-polarity witness would otherwise pass with flying colours.
field_guide.commit: Full 40-char commit SHA the path resolved at. Provenance, and the input to the historical-path resolver.
field_guide.origin_note: Human-readable version of commit plus path. Prose, never parsed.
field_guide.witnesses: What must be true of the materialised content for the fixture to be carrying the defect. Every literal is matched LITERALLY, as raw bytes, never as a regex and never executed.
field_guide.polarity: present when the literal must occur, absent when it must occur zero times. Both directions matter: C7 was widened to both polarities by decision 13-A, and M4 is the absent direction.
field_guide.count: Exact occurrence count. Only allowed on a blob-pinned file, where the content hash makes the number safe to freeze.
field_guide.lines: 1-based line numbers carrying the literal. Same rule as count, blob-pinned files only.

worktree_witnesses_carry_no_numbers: A witness on a worktree file may assert presence or absence and nothing more. Line numbers and counts are refused there by the validator, because freezing a number against content that is free to move would reintroduce the exact drift this check hunts. On a blob-pinned file the content hash makes those numbers permanent, so they are asserted.
